cards.body:
*Lesson 0.4 · Spreadsheets as Databases*

_≈ 100 minutes · with Miracle_

Most small-business automations read from and write to a spreadsheet. A sheet built for human eyes breaks automations; a sheet built like a database makes them almost easy. This module teaches the difference.

*Your problem:* Your records live in a spreadsheet that breaks as soon as it grows.
*The plan:* Rebuild a messy sheet as a tiny database with IDs, lookups and clean columns.
*After this lesson:* Your automations will have a reliable place to read and write data.

*Two Mrs Ades, one address*

*The files:* Three sheets. The same customer is called "Customer", "Name" and "Client". No automation can follow that.

*The mix-up:* Two different regulars share the same name. The sheet treats them as one person.

*The result:* Mokola's order arrives in Bodija. Another refund, another apology.

*The fix:* Weave, the octopus who'll guide Track 2, drops by to help Bolt redesign the sheets.

*The seven rules of an automation-friendly sheet*

- *1 · One header row*: Row 1 holds field names. Nothing above it: no title, no logo, no merged cells.
- *2 · One row = one record*: One order, one customer, one product. Never two in a row, never one across two rows.
- *3 · One column = one field, one type*: A "price" column holds only numbers. No "12,500 (discounted)".
- *4 · No gaps, no totals inside*: No blank rows, no subtotal rows. Put summaries on a separate tab.
- *5 · One table per tab*: Customers on one tab, orders on another. Not side by side.
- *6 · Colour is never data*: If yellow means VIP, add a `is_vip` column. Automations can't see colour.
- *7 · Every record has an ID*: A unique, never-changing code in column A.

*A good test:* could you export the tab as a CSV file and have it still make sense? If yes, an automation can use it.

*IDs: the name tag that never changes*

A *primary key* is a column whose value is unique for every row and never changes: `CUST-0015`, `HL-0043`, `TOM-CRATE`. When another table stores that ID to point back, it's called a *foreign key*.

*Bad IDs*

- *Names:* not unique (two Mrs Ades).
- *Phone numbers:* people change them and share them.
- *Row numbers:* change when you sort or delete.

*Good IDs*

- A short prefix that says what it is (`CUST-`, `HL-`).
- A padded counter so they sort correctly (`0015`, not `15`).
- Created once, by one process, never edited.

*Weave:* In Tracks 1–3 your automation will create IDs for you when a new order arrives. Until then, add them by hand and never reuse one, even for a deleted order.

*Relationships: one-to-many*

One customer places many orders. One order has many items. Each "many" side stores the ID of its "one" side. That's all a relational database is, and your sheet can do it.

*XLOOKUP and SUMIFS: reaching across tables*

*XLOOKUP* finds a value in one column and returns the matching value from another. It works in Google Sheets and current Excel.
Code example on screen (XLOOKUP and SUMIFS: reaching across tables): open it in the app.

*SUMIFS* adds up a column only for rows that match conditions. It's how a one-row order gets the total of its many items.

_(Code on screen in the app.)_

*Why not VLOOKUP?* VLOOKUP only looks to the right and breaks when someone inserts a column. You'll still see it in older sheets, so recognise it, but write XLOOKUP.

*Validation: stop bad data at the door*

Automations match text exactly. "Paid", "paid ", "PAID" and "yes" are four different values to a machine. *Data validation* restricts what can be typed.

- *Dropdown for status*: New · Paid · Out for delivery · Delivered · Cancelled. Nothing else is allowed.
- *Checkbox for yes/no*: Stores TRUE/FALSE, a real boolean.
- *Date rule*: "Is a valid date" stops "Tuesday" and "06/10".
- *Plain text for phones*: Format the column as plain text so the leading zero survives.

_Google Sheets · Airtable_
- *Feels like* · A familiar spreadsheet · A spreadsheet that behaves like a database
- *Linking tables* · By ID, with XLOOKUP and SUMIFS · Built-in "linked record" fields, plus lookups and rollups
- *Field types* · Enforced with validation rules · Each field has a fixed type from the start
- *Views* · Filters and filter views · Saved grid, kanban, calendar and form views
- *Best for* · Starting out, sharing with anyone, formulas · Growing operations, several linked tables, team workflows
- *Watch out* · People can type anywhere and break structure · The free plan has record and feature limits; check current terms

cards.body:
*Solved problem: rebuild Harvest Lane's order sheet*

*The problem.* Here's a slice of Tolu's current "Orders_final_2" tab. Redesign it so that every automation in the rest of this course can read and write it safely, and so the two Mrs Ades can never be confused again.

_A · B · C · D · E · F_
*1:* *HARVEST LANE ORDERS — OCTOBER!!!*
*2:* Client · Phone · Items · Amount · Paid? · Deliver
*3:* Mrs Adebayo · 8031234567 · 2 tomato, 1 tatashe · ₦35,500 · Paid · Tue
*4:* Mrs Ade · 8023456789 · 3 onions · 13500 · paid · 06/10
*5:* Mrs Ade · 8067654321 · 1 tomato · 14000 · YES · 7/10
*6:* *TOTAL WEEK 1* · 63,000
- 7
*8:* Mr Okafor · 8059876543 · 2 pepper · 18000 · 8 Oct

Red cells break a rule. Yellow rows mean "VIP" to Tolu, but only to Tolu.

*Step 1 · List what's wrong, rule by rule*

Title row above the headers (rule 1). Several products crammed into one "Items" cell (rule 2). "Amount" mixes text and numbers (rule 3). A total row and a blank row inside the data (rule 4). VIP shown by colour (rule 6). No IDs, so the two Mrs Ades are indistinguishable (rule 7). Plus: phones lost their zeros, "Paid?" has four spellings, and dates come in four formats.

*Step 2 · Split it into four linked tables*

Each thing that has its own identity gets its own tab: customers, products, orders, and the items inside orders. This mirrors the JSON from Module 0.3, where `items` was an array inside the order.

*Customers 1 row per customer*

- `customer_id`text · CUST-0007
- `name`text
- `phone`plain text · +234…
- `area`dropdown
- `is_vip`checkbox
- `lifetime_spend`formula

*Products 1 row per product*

- `sku`text · TOM-CRATE
- `name`text
- `unit`dropdown
- `price_ngn`number
- `stock_qty`number
- `active`checkbox

*Orders 1 row per order*

- `order_id`text · HL-0043
- `created_at`date-time
- `customer_id`→ Customers
- `customer_name`formula
- `delivery_date`date
- `delivery_fee`number
- `status`dropdown
- `items_total`formula
- `total`formula

*Order_Items 1 row per product in an order*

- `order_id`→ Orders
- `sku`→ Products
- `product_name`formula
- `qty`number
- `unit_price`number
- `line_total`formula

*Step 3 · Add the formulas*

Put each formula in row 2 and fill it down. The letters match the column order listed above.
Code example on screen (Add the formulas): open it in the app.

*Sage:* *Why unit_price is typed into Order_Items, not looked up:* prices change. If tomatoes go from ₦12,500 to ₦14,000 next month, last month's orders must still show what the customer actually paid. Look the price up _once_ when the order is created, then store it.

*Step 4 · Load the data and check the result*

Order HL-0043 from Module 0.3 becomes one Orders row and two Order_Items rows:

_order_id · customer_id · customer_name ƒ · delivery_date · fee · status · items_total ƒ · total ƒ_
- *HL-0043* · CUST-0007 · Mrs Adebayo · 2026-10-06 · 1500 · Paid · 34000 · *35500*

The total matches the hand calculation from 0.3 exactly. That's your proof the formulas are right.

*Step 5 · See why IDs fix the Mrs Ade problem*

Order HL-0045 belongs to the Mrs Ade who lives in Mokola. Switch between looking up by name and by ID, and pick different orders.
Hands-on lab: See why IDs fix the Mrs Ade problem. It's interactive, so open it in the app and try it there.

*Step 6 · Lock the inputs*

In Google Sheets: select the `status` column → *Data → Data validation* → Dropdown with the five status values → "Reject the input". Format `phone` as *Format → Number → Plain text*. Add checkboxes to `is_vip` and `active` with *Insert → Checkbox*. Finally, protect the formula columns (*Data → Protect sheets and ranges*) so nobody types over them.

*Why this approach works*

- Each table has one job and one kind of row.
- IDs make every link exact, whatever people are called.
- Totals are calculated, never typed, so they can't drift.
- Validation stops Glitch at the door instead of cleaning up later.

*Common mistakes to avoid*

- Looking up the _current_ price for old orders.
- Sorting one tab's columns separately and scrambling rows.
- Leaving room for "notes" in the middle of the data.
- Letting two processes both create IDs, causing duplicates.

*Glitch hunt*

*Glitch:* I built the Products tab myself. Every automation that touches it breaks. Find six problems.

_A · B · C · D · E_
*1:* sku · name · price · stock · active
*2:* TOM-CRATE · Tomatoes · 12500 · 40 · yes
*3:* TOM-CRATE · Tomatoes (small) · 7000 · 15 · Yes
*4:* Tatashe pepper · 9,000 / bag · 22 · y
*5:* ONI-BAG · Onions · 4000 · see Tolu · TRUE
*6:* PEP-TATASHE-L · Tatashe pepper · 9000 · 22 · TRUE

cards.prompt: Made your call on each one? Tap Reveal to check.
cards.answer:
1. *Duplicate ID:* rows 2 and 3 both use `TOM-CRATE`. Small crates need their own SKU, e.g. `TOM-CRATE-S`.
2. *Missing ID:* row 4 has no SKU at all.
3. *Duplicate record:* rows 4 and 6 are the same product twice. Keep one.
4. *Text in a number column:* "9,000 / bag" in `price`. The unit belongs in its own column.
5. *Text in a number column:* "see Tolu" in `stock`. Stock updates will crash on this row.
6. *Inconsistent booleans:* yes, Yes, y, TRUE. Replace the column with checkboxes.

cards.title: Bronze (+25 XP): Build a clean Customers table
cards.body:
- Create the Customers tab with 10 real or realistic customers, including two with the same name.
- IDs in `CUST-0001` style; phones as plain text with +234; area as a dropdown; VIP as a checkbox.
- Try to type "Bodja" in area and "08012" as text in a number column. Validation should reject both.

*Done when:*
- All seven rules pass, and the same-name customers have different IDs.

cards.title: Silver (+50 XP): Build all four tables and prove the totals
cards.body:
- Add Products, Orders and Order_Items with the formulas from the solved problem.
- Enter five orders, at least one with three items and one for each same-name customer.
- Check one order by hand against the formula total. Then set one order to Delivered and watch that customer's `lifetime_spend` change.

*Done when:*
- HL-0043 totals 35,500, no formula shows "Unknown", and lifetime spend counts delivered orders only.

cards.answer:
- *"Unknown customer":* the ID has a trailing space or different case. Copy IDs; don't retype them.
- *Total is 0:* a price or qty is stored as text. Check for ₦ or commas.
- *#REF!:* a tab was renamed. Tab names in formulas must match exactly.

cards.title: Gold (+100 XP): Build it again in Airtable and compare
cards.body:
- Create a free Airtable base with the same four tables, using linked records instead of IDs-with-XLOOKUP.
- Use a *rollup* for `items_total` and a formula for `total`.
- Create a kanban view of Orders grouped by status, and a form view for new orders.
- Write half a page: which would you give Tolu today, and when should Harvest Lane switch?

*Done when:*
- Both builds produce the same totals, and your recommendation names a specific trigger for switching (volume, number of staff, or number of linked tables).

cards.answer: Start Tolu on Google Sheets: free, familiar, and every platform in this course connects to it. Switch to Airtable when more than two people edit orders daily, or when Tolu needs a kanban board for riders; linked records and locked field types will prevent the errors that start once more hands touch the data. At much higher volume, move to a real database like Supabase (Track 4).

cards.q: Which makes the best primary key for a customer?
cards.why: Names repeat, phones change, row numbers move when you sort. A generated code is unique and permanent.

cards.q: An order contains three different products. Where does it live?
options: One row, with all products in an "Items" cell
One row in Orders and three rows in Order_Items
cards.why: One row per thing: the order once, and each product line once, linked by order_id.

cards.q: Why store `unit_price` on each Order_Items row instead of always looking it up?
options: Prices change, and old orders must keep the price actually charged
It makes the sheet load faster
cards.why: History must not change when today's price does.

cards.q: In `=XLOOKUP(C2, Customers!A:A, Customers!B:B, "Unknown customer")`, what does the last part do?
options: Shows that text when no match is found
cards.why: It's the fallback. A visible 'Unknown customer' is much easier to spot than an error code.

options: A status dropdown with fixed values
A weekly total row under each week's orders
A merged title row above the headers
cards.why: Fixed values can be matched exactly. Colour, total rows and title rows all break automations.

cards.body:
*Remember this*

1. One header row, one record per row, one type per column, one table per tab.
2. No totals, gaps or colour-as-meaning inside the data.
3. Every record gets a unique, permanent ID. Names are for people.
4. One-to-many: the "many" table stores the ID of the "one".
5. XLOOKUP reaches across tables; SUMIFS totals the many into the one.
6. Validate inputs; store prices at the time of sale.

*Lesson 0.4 complete!* _Spreadsheets as Databases_ is done and saved to your progress, on WhatsApp and in the app.

Next up: Lesson 0.5, _Talking to AI: LLM Essentials_.
